questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Mainly my interest in Australian literature, art, history and the nature. And the University of Melbourne had some unique and interesting courses as well.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy. As with everything you have to take time to look into it but the information was easy to find and navigate in.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The University had an introduction with a lot of useful information and a pre-depature meeting on zoom as well. I felt very safe and guided when arriving at the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The housing was easy enough to find but quite expensive, even the ones designed for students.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can make it a bit harder to find friends, as a lot of connections are often made through shared housing experiences, but of course that also depends one the individual persons effort to seek out people .

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy. You just had to follow a very detailed guide online, and there was a lot of steps, but most of it made sense and information for who to contact if you needed help was easy to find as well.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could contact the university per email, but all parts of the process was also explained in detail online.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes i wanted. At the university of Melbourne the offer a lot of classes in the same subject, so you have to be very unlucky if you don't get the ones you want.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just read through everything carefully, don't stress, and keep your cool. Everything will work out and if you are afraid you might be doing something wrong, you probably are not. And if you are, they will contact you and help you out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: All of my courses where MA courses

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was a combination of lectures and classes where you discussed the writings with your fellow students. Less lecture style than I am used to from UCPH. There were more assignments doing the semester then I was used too, but the teaches were very helpful in providing guidance and stating what they wanted from the students.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
History of Books and Reading
International Publishing
Writing about Art and the Moving Image
Mobility, Culture and Communication

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Just choose the ones that you think sounds fun, honestly. But I did really love History of Books and Reading a lot - our teacher was the best and the course was interesting.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to pay for a health check for my visa before going, but most people are not asked to do this, so it is not a cost for everyone. it was around 3500 DKK, the visa was 3200 DKK in addition.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing, food, transportation

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just about anything you could want

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join a club to meet people, but also get out and see the city and the nature outside of Melbourne. It is easiest to get out of the city if you have a car, but the city and suburbs are easy to get around in with public transportation

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: It depends on what people like of course, I enjoyed the galleries, museum, the food culture and the beautiful seaside and the forests outside of Melbourne

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None at all

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are very helpful and open, and it is a very diverse country compared to Denmark

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Try to make friends, it will make studying much more fun
2) Don't only study. It might seem like you have to work extra hard and that the teachers expect a lot from you. But the level is actually quite similar to that of UCPH
3) You come a long way with asking the university for help in any aspect, not only school work. They have al sorts of help if you are struggling to find friends, or feel lonely.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people, exploring a ned city and country

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Trusting that I was doing well enough in the classes even though english is not my first language

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
